assumptions: steady flow, fixed temperature and composition
text: When the time for chain relaxation is short compared with the deformation time, increasing a small shear rate can increase the shear stress nearly proportionally. Use a plateau only when the measured rate range supports one.

assumptions: fixed composition and temperature; steady simple shear
text: A declining steady shear viscosity with rate need not imply declining shear stress. Viscosity is the ratio to the imposed shear rate. The trend should be checked on a single matched flow curve.

assumptions: check whether composition, phase state and method remain comparable
valid_range: temperature interval established for the same polymer
text: Some polymer melts become less viscous when temperature rises. Compare steady values at matched rates and inspect nearby transitions before treating this as a quantitative correction.

assumptions: fixed filler shape, interface and matrix
text: Particles can restrict polymer motion and add to the stress. The trend can depend on the interface, dispersion and aggregation, so filler fraction alone is insufficient to transfer a measured size of the effect to another material.

assumptions: LAMMPS pressure sign and registered steady window
text: Use the sign convention of the simulator when computing viscosity from shear stress. Report the stress definition and sampling window before comparing tables. A reduced viscosity requires a specified unit conversion to compare with Pa s.

Apparent capillary viscosity can reflect entrance pressure losses or slip at the wall. Treat agreement with periodic molecular simulation as a separate hypothesis unless the bulk shear response is identified.
